open_questions: Are the three transit depths statistically consistent after accounting for spot occultations and pipeline systematics?
Do additional sectors or RV rule out odd/even depth difference and confirm the transit is not a grazing background eclipsing binary?
Is the dip exactly on-target with a precise centroid and a non-grazing light-curve shape?
dossier.public_summary: A shallow 3.8 Earth-radius dip repeats every 9.02 days with a duration that fits the host star and shows no secondary eclipse. The signal is seen in only three closely spaced transits, their depths disagree, and odd transits look deeper than even ones at moderate significance, while a centroid cannot yet prove the source is the target star. More transits and a sky position measurement are needed to separate a grazing planet transit from a blended small-star eclipse.

reasons.why: Difference approaches the 4-sigma binary threshold and is the largest sector odd/even signal. Likely spot-crossing modulation but statistically significant enough to need confirmation that odd/even are consistent.
reasons.value: diff_sigma 2.427, depth_difference 0.3839 (odd 2861 ppm vs even 1763 ppm)

reasons.why: Scorer rates this well below the median planet (0.5) and in the range where false positives dominate, supporting caution rather than a clean planet.
Only three transits in one sector show formally inconsistent depths, so the measured odd/even difference and any density/shape mismatch cannot be averaged out and must be validated.
No centroid image can localize the dip to the target; together with a grazing fit (fit_b 0.9599) and star_density_penalty 5.157 it leaves a blended V-shaped eclipse as plausible.

Radius is planet-sized and duration fits a central transit on the K-dwarf (TIC rad 0.7434 FLAME 0.765 rad), but a grazing geometry gives the same size so shape and density alone do not rule out a small stellar eclipse.
reasons.value: rp_rearth 3.825, duration ratio 1.131, shape v_sigma 1.384, fit_b 0.9599, star_density_penalty 5.157
